description: A three-panel composite figure of crystal-structure models (ball-and-stick unit cells) contrasting the atomic arrangements of the austenitic and κ-carbide phases in FCC Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys. (a) Disordered γ: a cube with two visually distinct sphere species — light grey and dark filled — occupying both corner and face-centre sites without regular alternation, i.e. Fe/Mn and Al randomly distributed on FCC lattice positions; dashed body-diagonal lines mark the octahedral geometry. (b) Ordered γ, L1₂: the same cube but grey hatched spheres now strictly at the eight corners and black spheres at the six face centres; a lower-right legend labels the black sphere "Fe/Mn". (c) κ-carbide: corner (grey hatched = "Al") and face-centre ("Fe/Mn" black) occupancies as in (b), plus an extra small black dot labelled "C" at the body centre — the octahedral interstitial site made by Fe and Mn. Legends are given only in (b) and (c); panel (a) carries no colour key. Together the panels show that successive ordering — Al to corners, Fe/Mn to faces, then C to the body centre — converts disordered γ into ordered L1₂ and finally into perovskite-type κ-carbide (Fe,Mn)₃AlC. No numeric values, scale bars or composition figures are printed anywhere in the images.

observations.observation: Panel (a) shows a cubic unit cell in which two visually different sphere species (light grey and dark filled) appear on both corner and face-centre sites with no regular alternation.
Panel (b) shows grey hatched spheres exclusively at the eight corner sites and black spheres exclusively at the six face-centre sites of the cube.
The legend printed inside panel (b) labels the black sphere as 'Fe/Mn'.
The legend printed inside panel (c) labels the grey hatched sphere as 'Al' and the small black dot as 'C'.
Panel (c) contains an extra small sphere at the geometric centre (body centre) of the cube that is absent from panels (a) and (b).
Dashed lines indicating the body-diagonal/octahedral interstitial geometry are drawn in panels (a) and (b); panel (a) carries no legend or species key.
No numerical values, axis ticks, scale bars or composition labels are printed in any of the three panels.
The caption identifies the three panels as unit cells of disordered γ (a), ordered γ, L1₂ (b) and κ-carbide (c) structure in FCC alloys.

The caption states that in the illustrated κ-carbide with ideal stoichiometry Al occupies each corner, Fe and Mn are located on the face centres and the C atom sits at the centre of the unit cell, which is also an octahedral site made by Fe and Mn.
The citing text states that the κ-phase has a perovskite crystal structure designated as E2₁ in the Strukturbericht classification.
The citing text states that κ-carbide with ideal stoichiometry is (Fe,Mn)₃AlC.
The citing text states that further ordering of C to the body-centre octahedral interstitial position produces the κ-carbide, as seen in Fig. 6c.
The citing text states that a metastable (Fe,Mn)₃AlC_x (x < 1) phase with the same crystal structure as the κ phase but incomplete occupation of the C atoms may form via spinodal decomposition.

The citing text states that atom probe tomography of a Fe-30Mn-7.7Al-1.3C alloy aged at 600 °C for 24 h indicates depletion of both interstitial C and substitutional Al compared with the ideal stoichiometric bulk perovskite.

subfigures.description: Unit cell illustrating disordered γ: a cube drawn with dashed body-diagonal lines, containing two distinct sphere types (light grey and dark filled) placed at both corner and face-centre positions in no regular order, representing randomly located Fe/Mn and Al atoms in an FCC lattice. No legend or site labels are provided in this panel.

Unit cell of ordered γ (L1₂): grey hatched spheres occupy all eight cube corners and solid black spheres occupy the six face centres, with dashed lines marking the body-diagonal/octahedral geometry. A legend at the lower right shows a black sphere labelled 'Fe/Mn'.

Unit cell of the κ-carbide: identical arrangement to (b) — grey hatched spheres (= Al) at the corners, black spheres (= Fe/Mn) at the face centres — with an additional small black sphere placed at the centre of the unit cell (= C). Legend at bottom left: grey hatched sphere = 'Al', small black dot = 'C'; the black face-centre sphere corresponds to 'Fe/Mn' as in (b).

unreadable_items: Panel (a) has no legend or colour key, so which sphere species corresponds to Fe/Mn versus Al must be inferred from the caption/citing text rather than read from the panel.
The supplied caption text is garbled by subscript/OCR corruption (e.g. 'j-carbide' where κ-carbide is meant, and interleaved fragments), so its exact original wording cannot be fully reconstructed.
